# Task 2: gRNA design for OAS2

```{r task2-setup}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

consensus_table <- readRDS("data/consensus_table.rds")
```

## Target gene selection

Task 1 identified six genes that were significant in both DESeq2 and edgeR. Both methods also agreed on the direction of the expression change. The six consensus genes are shown in @tbl-consensus.

For Task 2, we selected **OAS2** (`ENSG00000111335`). OAS2 showed a strong increase in expression in the SARS condition with both differential-expression methods. It also has a clear role in the human antiviral response. OAS2 is part of the interferon-induced OAS pathway and contributes to activation of RNase L after viral double-stranded RNA is detected [@merold2025]. OAS family genes have also been linked to severe COVID-19 and COVID-19-related heart failure [@gao2023; @hernandezramirez2026].

The Task 1 result for OAS2 is summarised in @tbl-oas2-de.

```{r tbl-oas2-de}
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Differential-expression results for OAS2 from Task 1."

consensus_table |>
  filter(gene_name == "OAS2") |> 
  select(fold_change_deseq, adj_p_value_deseq, fold_change_edger, adj_p_value_edger) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = c(".value", "Method"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_(deseq|edger)"
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    Method = recode_values(
      Method,
      "deseq" ~ "DESeq2",
      "edger" ~ "edgeR-LRT"
    )
  ) |> 
  dplyr::rename(
    `Fold change` = fold_change,
    `Adjusted p-value / FDR` = adj_p_value
  ) |> 
  kable(
    digits = 3,
    align = c("l", "r", "r")
  )
```

OAS2 had a DESeq2 log2 fold change of **9.90** and an edgeR logFC of **10.30**. Both values are positive. This shows strong upregulation in the SARS samples compared with mock.

## Choice of CRISPR strategy

The project hypothesis is that restoring deregulated gene expression may improve recovery. Because OAS2 was strongly upregulated, we selected **CRISPR interference (CRISPRi)** rather than CRISPR activation. CRISPRi uses catalytically inactive Cas9 together with a transcriptional repressor such as KRAB to reduce transcription [@jensen2021].

The project asks us to design guides within the **first exon** of the selected gene. We therefore identified the first exon of the OAS2 MANE Select transcript and used this sequence for guide design.

## OAS2 transcript selection

OAS2 was inspected in Ensembl using the human **GRCh38.p14** reference assembly. The gene is located on chromosome 12 and is on the forward strand.

The **MANE Select transcript `ENST00000392583.7`** was selected. MANE provides a representative transcript that is matched between NCBI and EMBL-EBI [@morales2022].

![OAS2 gene view in Ensembl. The MANE Select transcript `ENST00000392583.7` is shown for the protein-coding OAS2 gene on chromosome 12.](figures/task2/OAS2_ensembl.png){#fig-oas2-ensembl width="95%"}

## Selection of the first exon

The MANE Select transcript contains 10 exons. The first exon is **`ENSE00002421397.2`**. It is located at `chr12:112,978,519-112,978,785`, is on the forward strand, and has a length of **267 bp**.

![First exon of the OAS2 MANE Select transcript. Exon 1 (`ENSE00002421397.2`) is 267 bp long and was used for guide design.](figures/task2/OAS2_Selection%20of%20the%20first%20exon%20of%20OAS2.png){#fig-oas2-first-exon width="95%"}

The first-exon sequence was copied from Ensembl and used as the input sequence for CRISPOR.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## Guide design with CRISPOR

Several guide-design tools are available, including SSC, E-CRISP, CHOPCHOP and CRISPOR [@li2023; @cui2018]. We selected **CRISPOR** because it reports predicted guide efficiency, specificity scores and possible off-target sites. It also provides genomic locations for predicted off-targets and allows the results to be downloaded for later analysis [@concordet2018].

The CRISPOR analysis used the following settings:

-   **Reference genome:** Homo sapiens GRCh38/hg38
-   **Target sequence:** first exon of OAS2 (`ENSE00002421397.2`)
-   **Nuclease:** SpCas9
-   **PAM:** NGG
-   **Guide length:** 20 bp

![CRISPOR input settings used for the OAS2 first exon. The human GRCh38/hg38 reference genome and the 20bp-NGG SpCas9 PAM setting were selected.](figures/task2/crispr_settings.png){#fig-crispor-settings width="95%"}

After submitting the sequence, CRISPOR returned the SpCas9-compatible guides within the first exon. The output includes specificity scores, several predicted efficiency scores and predicted off-target sites.

![CRISPOR candidate guides for the first exon of OAS2. The table shows guide position, sequence, specificity scores, predicted efficiency scores and off-target information.](figures/task2/crispr_results_table.png){#fig-crispor-results width="100%"}

## Selected guide RNAs

Two guides were selected from the CRISPOR output. We considered both predicted efficiency and specificity. Their main CRISPOR values are shown in @tbl-selected-guides.

```{r tbl-selected-guides}
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Selected OAS2 guide RNAs and CRISPOR prediction scores."

guide_table <- tribble(
  ~Guide, ~Position, ~Protospacer, ~PAM, ~`MIT specificity`, ~`CFD specificity`, ~`Doench 2016`, ~`Moreno-Mateos`, ~`RuleSet3`, ~`Predicted off-targets`,
  "gRNA 1", "200/fw", "TCAGACACTGATCGACGAGA", "TGG", 97, 96, 64, 48, 44, 52,
  "gRNA 2", "248/fw", "GGAACCCGAACAGTTCCCCC", "TGG", 89, 96, 55, 27, 89, 52
)

guide_table |>
  kable(
    align = c("l", "l", "l", "c", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r")
  )
```

gRNA 1 had the higher MIT specificity score (**97**). gRNA 2 had the higher RuleSet3 efficiency score (**89**). Both guides had a CFD specificity score of **96**.

CRISPOR reported **52 possible off-target sites** for each guide. For gRNA 1, the off-target distribution was `0-0-0-4-48` for sites with 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 mismatches. For gRNA 2, the distribution was `0-0-0-5-47`. Therefore, no perfect, one-mismatch or two-mismatch off-target was reported in the displayed results.

These values are predictions. They are useful for comparing guide candidates, but they do not prove how well a guide will work experimentally.

## Preparation for Task 3

The selected guides and their off-target information can now be carried forward to Task 3. The next step is to check whether genetic variants in individual genomes change the guide target sequence or alter possible off-target sites.

## Task 2 conclusion

OAS2 was selected from the six Task 1 consensus genes because it showed strong and consistent upregulation in both DESeq2 and edgeR and has a clear role in the antiviral response. CRISPRi was selected to reduce its expression. The MANE Select transcript `ENST00000392583.7` was used to identify the 267 bp first exon. CRISPOR was then used with the GRCh38/hg38 reference genome and SpCas9-NGG settings. Two candidate guides at positions **200/fw** and **248/fw** were selected based on their predicted efficiency and specificity. These guides will be used in Task 3.
